ex: Gli allibratori davano la squadra sfavorita a dieci contro uno.
exEn: The bookmakers had the underdogs at ten to one.
note: Betting/journalistic; from 'allibrare' (to enter in a book). The English 'bookmaker' is also current; 'ricevitoria' is the betting shop.

ex: Il biscazziere raccoglieva le puntate con la sigaretta all'angolo della bocca.
exEn: The gambling-den keeper collected the stakes with a cigarette in the corner of his mouth.
note: Literary/dated, pejorative; from 'bisca' (illegal gambling den). Also used of a compulsive gambler.

ex: Da grande passista, tirò il gruppo per cinquanta chilometri di pianura.
exEn: Being a great rouleur, he pulled the bunch for fifty kilometres of flat road.
note: Cycling jargon; the taxonomy of riders: 'scalatore' (climber), 'velocista' (sprinter), 'passista', 'cronoman' (time-triallist), 'gregario' (domestique).

ex: Il corridore si lasciò scivolare indietro fino all'ammiraglia per prendere le borracce.
exEn: The rider dropped back to the team car to collect the water bottles.
note: Cycling jargon, from 'nave ammiraglia' (flagship); also of a company's flagship product ('il modello ammiraglia').

ex: Il trequartista si muoveva tra le linee, dove nessun difensore riusciva a marcarlo.
exEn: The number ten drifted between the lines, where no defender could mark him.
note: Football jargon, from 'tre quarti' (three-quarters of the pitch); roles in Italian tactical language: 'regista', 'mezzala', 'terzino', 'centravanti'.

en: psychological subservience (referees' bias towards big clubs)
ex: Il rigore non concesso ha riacceso le accuse di sudditanza psicologica verso le grandi squadre.
exEn: The penalty that was not given revived accusations of psychological subservience towards the big clubs.
note: Italian football-journalism cliché; 'sudditanza' alone (subjection) is a formal political term.

ex: I due sfidanti si affrontarono in singolar tenzone davanti a tutto il torneo.
exEn: The two challengers faced each other in single combat in front of the whole tournament.
note: Archaic/literary (chivalric romance), now used jocularly of sports duels and political face-offs; 'tenzone' = poetic contest or fight.

en: roll of honour; list of past winners
ex: Con questa vittoria il club entra per la prima volta nell'albo d'oro della coppa.
exEn: With this win the club enters the cup's roll of honour for the first time.
note: Sports journalism; 'albo' = register. Cf. 'palmarès' (an individual's list of wins), 'medagliere' (medal table).

ex: Il capovoga alzò il ritmo a trentotto colpi negli ultimi cinquecento metri.
exEn: The stroke raised the rate to thirty-eight in the last five hundred metres.
note: Rowing jargon; irregular plural 'capivoga'. 'Voga' = rowing stroke; the cox is 'timoniere'; the bow rower 'prodiere'.

ex: Una strambata involontaria fece passare il boma a un palmo dalla sua testa.
exEn: An accidental gybe sent the boom a hand's breadth from his head.
note: Sailing; turning with the wind astern, as opposed to 'virata' (tack, through the wind). Verb 'strambare'.

ex: Il siepista azzurro è caduto alla riviera all'ultimo giro.
exEn: The Italian steeplechaser fell at the water jump on the last lap.
note: Athletics jargon, from 'siepi' (the 3000 m steeplechase, 'tremila siepi'). Cf. 'ostacolista' (hurdler).

ex: Nei carruggi di Genova il sole arriva a terra solo a mezzogiorno.
exEn: In Genoa's alleys the sun reaches the ground only at midday.
note: Ligurian regionalism, also 'caruggio'; the Venetian equivalent is 'calle', the general term 'vicolo'.

ex: Passato il sottoportego, la calle sbuca all'improvviso su un campo silenzioso.
exEn: Beyond the covered passage, the alley suddenly opens onto a quiet little square.
note: Venetian toponymic term (also 'sotoportego'); standard 'sottoportico'. Part of the Venice set: 'calle', 'campo', 'rio', 'fondamenta', 'salizada'.

en: medieval town hall with a balcony for public speeches
ex: Dal balcone dell'arengario il podestà leggeva le sentenze alla folla.
exEn: From the balcony of the arengario the podestà read the sentences to the crowd.
note: Historical/architectural (Monza, Milan, Novara); from 'arengo' (assembly), same root as 'arringa' (harangue).

en: postern; small secondary gate in a city wall
ex: I congiurati uscirono di notte da una postierla nascosta dietro il convento.
exEn: The conspirators slipped out at night through a postern hidden behind the convent.
note: Historical/architectural; Milan still names streets 'Pusterla'. Cf. 'porta' (main gate), 'pusterla' (Lombard variant).

ex: Il barbacane proteggeva la porta principale dagli assalti diretti.
exEn: The barbican protected the main gate from direct assaults.
note: Military architecture; also a buttress or a projecting upper storey in Venetian houses. Cf. 'baluardo', 'bastione', 'rivellino'.

ex: Lungo la costa si vedono ancora le casematte in cemento della seconda guerra mondiale.
exEn: Along the coast you can still see the concrete pillboxes of the Second World War.
note: Military architecture; plural 'casematte'. Cf. 'bunker' (borrowed), 'fortino' (small fort).

ex: Le caditoie intasate di foglie hanno trasformato la strada in un torrente.
exEn: The storm drains, blocked with leaves, turned the street into a torrent.
note: Technical: municipal/road engineering (also 'tombino', 'chiusino') and castle architecture (opening for dropping projectiles).

en: third (historical district of a city divided into three)
ex: Siena è divisa in tre terzieri, ognuno dei quali comprende diverse contrade.
exEn: Siena is divided into three terzieri, each of which contains several contrade.
note: Historical/toponymic; parallel to 'sestiere' (Venice, Genoa), 'quartiere' (Florence), 'rione' (Rome).

en: projecting front section of a building
ex: L'avancorpo centrale del palazzo è scandito da quattro colonne giganti.
exEn: The central projecting bay of the palace is articulated by four giant columns.
note: Architectural (French 'avant-corps'); the 'corpo di fabbrica' is the building block, 'ala' a wing, 'prospetto' the elevation.

ex: Un cippo di marmo ricorda i partigiani fucilati in quel crocevia.
exEn: A marble memorial stone commemorates the partisans shot at that crossroads.
note: Formal/monumental ('cippo funerario', 'cippo confinario'); Latinism (cippus). Cf. 'lapide' (plaque), 'stele' (upright slab).

en: hinny (offspring of a horse and a she-ass)
ex: Il bardotto è più piccolo del mulo e molto più raro.
exEn: The hinny is smaller than the mule and much rarer.
note: Zootechnical; 'mulo' = donkey father and mare, 'bardotto' = stallion and she-ass. Figurative (dated): a hanger-on who travels free.

ex: Per i principianti il maneggio usa solo castroni, più docili degli stalloni.
exEn: For beginners the riding school uses only geldings, which are gentler than stallions.
note: Zootechnical; also a castrated ram. 'Castroneria' (colloquial) = a blunder, nonsense.

ex: Il carretto era tirato da una brenna che a ogni salita sembrava dover crollare.
exEn: The cart was pulled by a nag that seemed about to collapse on every slope.
note: Literary/colloquial, pejorative; near-synonyms 'ronzino', 'rozza'. Also a jocular insult for a poor athlete.

ex: Un saettone lungo un metro e mezzo attraversò il sentiero senza fretta.
exEn: An Aesculapian snake a metre and a half long crossed the path unhurriedly.
note: Herpetology/regional (from 'saetta', arrow, for its speed); also 'colubro di Esculapio'. Non-venomous, unlike 'vipera', 'marasso', 'aspide'.

ex: L'orbettino sembra un serpente ma è una lucertola senza zampe.
exEn: The slow-worm looks like a snake but is a legless lizard.
note: Zoology; from 'orbo' (blind), a folk belief. Regional names abound ('cecella', 'lucignolo').

ex: Al crepuscolo il succiacapre emette il suo lungo trillo ronzante.
exEn: At dusk the nightjar gives its long, whirring trill.
note: Ornithology; invariable compound (succhiare + capre), from the ancient belief that it suckled goats. Also 'nottolone'.

ex: Il capovaccaio è il più piccolo e il più minacciato degli avvoltoi italiani.
exEn: The Egyptian vulture is the smallest and most endangered of Italy's vultures.
note: Ornithology; Italian vultures: 'grifone' (griffon), 'gipeto' (bearded vulture), 'avvoltoio monaco', 'capovaccaio'.

ex: La macchia bassa era un intrico di lentisco, mirto e cisto.
exEn: The low scrub was a tangle of mastic, myrtle and rockrose.
note: Botany (Pistacia lentiscus), typical of Sardinia and the South; its resin is 'mastice'. Companion shrubs: 'mirto', 'cisto', 'corbezzolo'.

ex: Il vivaista riproduce i vecchi olivi per margotta piuttosto che per talea.
exEn: The nurseryman propagates the old olive trees by air layering rather than by cuttings.
note: Horticulture; verb 'margottare'. Propagation methods: 'talea' (cutting), 'innesto' (graft), 'propaggine' (ground layering), 'margotta'.

ex: Il poeta cantava l'ubertà dei campi e la dovizia dei raccolti.
exEn: The poet sang of the fertility of the fields and the abundance of the harvests.
note: Literary Latinism (ubertas); adjective 'ubertoso'. Neutral 'fertilità', 'abbondanza'.

ex: Il discorso fu una sequela di luoghi comuni e di cifre sbagliate.
exEn: The speech was a string of clichés and wrong figures.
note: Formal, slightly pejorative; 'una sequela di insulti/errori'. Medical plural 'sequele' = after-effects. Neutral 'serie', 'sfilza' (colloquial).

ex: La carrozza era tirata da una pariglia di bai perfettamente uguali.
exEn: The carriage was drawn by a pair of perfectly matched bays.
note: Equestrian/literary; alive in 'rendere la pariglia' (to pay someone back in kind). Neutral 'paio', 'coppia'.

ex: Il contadino doveva al padrone dieci staia di grano l'anno.
exEn: The peasant owed the landowner ten bushels of wheat a year.
note: Historical measure (roughly 18-25 litres by region); plural 'le staia' (feminine) or 'gli stai'. Biblical 'mettere la lucerna sotto lo staio'.

en: modius; old measure of grain or land
ex: Il podere misurava trenta moggia, secondo il catasto borbonico.
exEn: The farm measured thirty moggia, according to the Bourbon land register.
note: Historical (Latin modius); plural 'le moggia' (feminine) or 'i moggi'. Still met in southern deeds and dialects.

en: tarì (old Sicilian and Neapolitan gold coin)
ex: Il mercante pagò il carico di seta in tarì d'oro coniati ad Amalfi.
exEn: The merchant paid for the cargo of silk in gold tarì minted at Amalfi.
note: Numismatics/history (from Arabic); invariable. Old Italian coins: 'fiorino', 'ducato', 'zecchino', 'scudo', 'baiocco', 'grano'.

ex: Si offende per un nonnulla e poi tiene il broncio per giorni.
exEn: He takes offence at the slightest thing and then sulks for days.
note: Formal/literary; 'nonnulla' is an invariable masculine noun used almost only with 'un'. Near-synonyms 'un'inezia', 'una bazzecola', 'una quisquilia'.

ex: Le ore, i minuti e i gradi seguono ancora il sistema sessagesimale dei Babilonesi.
exEn: Hours, minutes and degrees still follow the Babylonians' sexagesimal system.
note: Mathematical/technical; contrasted with 'decimale' and 'centesimale' (gradians, in surveying).

ex: Il prelato ridacchiava e la pappagorgia gli tremolava sul colletto.
exEn: The prelate chuckled and his double chin wobbled over his collar.
note: Literary/jocular; from 'pappa' + 'gorgia' (throat). Neutral 'doppio mento'; 'bazza' is a jutting chin.

ex: Sorrise mostrando una chiostra di denti bianchissimi.
exEn: She smiled, showing a set of dazzling white teeth.
note: Literary: 'chiostra di denti' (Dante uses 'chiostra' for a walled enclosure). Neutral 'dentatura'.

ex: La canizie precoce gli dava un'aria autorevole già a quarant'anni.
exEn: His premature white hair gave him an authoritative look already at forty.
note: Literary Latinism (canities), invariable; adjective 'canuto'. Neutral 'capelli bianchi'.

en: mop of hair; long unkempt hair
ex: Con quella zazzera bionda sembrava un cantante degli anni Settanta.
exEn: With that blond mop he looked like a seventies singer.
note: Colloquial-literary; 'zazzeruto' = with long hair. Cf. 'chioma' (neutral/literary, flowing hair), 'criniera' (mane).

ex: Il nemico volse le terga e si diede alla fuga.
exEn: The enemy turned tail and fled.
note: Literary plural (singular 'tergo', masculine, used in 'a tergo' = on the back/overleaf); 'volgere le terga' = to turn one's back, retreat.

en: lunula (white crescent at the base of a nail)
ex: La lunula è più visibile sui pollici che sulle altre dita.
exEn: The lunula is more visible on the thumbs than on the other fingers.
note: Anatomical; Latin diminutive of 'luna'. Also the crescent-shaped ornament in archaeology.

ex: Parlava a singulti, interrompendosi a ogni parola per riprendere fiato.
exEn: He spoke in sobs, breaking off at every word to catch his breath.
note: Literary for 'singhiozzo' (sob) and medical for hiccup ('singulto persistente'). Everyday word: 'singhiozzo' for both.

ex: Giunse in cima con un anelito affannoso, senza poter dire una parola.
exEn: He reached the top gasping for breath, unable to say a word.
note: Literary; both physical (laboured breath) and figurative ('anelito di libertà' = yearning for freedom). Verb 'anelare'.

ex: La nonna curava il raffreddore con suffumigi di bicarbonato e foglie di eucalipto.
exEn: Grandma treated colds with steam inhalations of bicarbonate and eucalyptus leaves.
note: Home-remedy vocabulary, usually plural; also 'fumenti'. Latin 'suffumigare'. Medical term 'inalazione'.

ex: La notizia del licenziamento fu accolta con sbigottimento generale.
exEn: The news of the dismissal was received with general dismay.
note: Formal; adjective 'sbigottito', verb 'sbigottire'. Near-synonyms: 'sgomento' (dread-tinged), 'costernazione' (grief), 'stupore' (surprise).

ex: L'irresolutezza del comandante costò alla flotta la giornata.
exEn: The commander's irresoluteness cost the fleet the day.
note: Formal/literary; adjective 'irresoluto'. Cf. 'indecisione' (neutral), 'titubanza', 'tentennamento' (wavering).

ex: Dopo il lutto cadde in un'abulia da cui nemmeno il lavoro riusciva a scuoterlo.
exEn: After the bereavement he sank into an abulia from which not even work could rouse him.
note: Psychological/literary (Greek); adjective 'abulico'. Stronger and more clinical than 'apatia'; 'accidia' is the moral-theological sloth.

ex: Sopportò le offese del fratello con una longanimità che rasentava la santità.
exEn: He bore his brother's insults with a forbearance that bordered on sainthood.
note: Literary/religious Latinism (longanimitas); adjective 'longanime'. Neutral 'pazienza', 'tolleranza'.

ex: Il giudice ascoltò entrambe le parti con la stessa equanimità.
exEn: The judge listened to both sides with the same equanimity.
note: Formal; in Italian it stresses impartiality as much as calm. Adjective 'equanime'. Cf. 'imperturbabilità' (unflappability), 'atarassia' (philosophical).

ex: I moralisti del Seicento vedevano nella concupiscenza la radice di ogni peccato.
exEn: Seventeenth-century moralists saw concupiscence as the root of every sin.
note: Theological/literary; now often ironic. Near-synonyms by register: 'libidine', 'lussuria' (sin), 'bramosia' (greedy longing).

ex: La sua ombrosità rendeva difficile fargli qualsiasi osservazione.
exEn: His touchiness made it hard to make any remark to him at all.
note: Formal; adjective 'ombroso', originally of a horse that shies at shadows. Cf. 'permalosità' (quick to take offence), 'suscettibilità'.

ex: Il vecchio, iracondo e sordo, urlava contro chiunque entrasse nel cortile.
exEn: The old man, wrathful and deaf, shouted at anyone who came into the yard.
note: Literary Latinism; noun 'iracondia'. Dante's 'iracondi' in Inferno VII. Neutral 'irascibile', 'collerico'.

ex: Entrò giulivo nella stanza, ignaro del disastro che lo aspettava.
exEn: He walked blithely into the room, unaware of the disaster awaiting him.
note: Literary, today mostly ironic ('tutto giulivo'); 'giulivo' suggests naive, slightly foolish cheer. Neutral 'allegro', 'lieto'.

en: abduction (inference to the best explanation); abduction (anatomy)
ex: Sherlock Holmes procede per abduzione, non per deduzione: dagli indizi risale all'ipotesi più plausibile.
exEn: Sherlock Holmes reasons by abduction, not deduction: from the clues he works back to the most plausible hypothesis.
note: Logic/philosophy of science (Peirce) and anatomy (movement away from the midline, opposite 'adduzione'). Not the crime sense of English 'abduction' (Italian 'rapimento').

ex: L'associazione tra caffè e infarto era dovuta al confondimento del fumo.
exEn: The association between coffee and heart attack was due to confounding by smoking.
note: Epidemiological/statistical jargon: 'fattore di confondimento' = confounder. Everyday 'confusione' is not used in this sense.

ex: La brina si forma per brinamento del vapore acqueo, senza passare per lo stato liquido.
exEn: Frost forms by deposition of water vapour, without passing through the liquid state.
note: Physics/meteorology; the reverse of 'sublimazione'. From 'brina' (hoar-frost).

ex: Oltre il carico di snervamento l'acciaio si deforma in modo permanente.
exEn: Beyond the yield load the steel deforms permanently.
note: Engineering ('tensione di snervamento'); everyday 'snervante' means exhausting, unrelated in use.

en: nutation (wobble of a rotation axis; nodding of plants)
ex: La nutazione sovrappone alla precessione terrestre una piccola oscillazione di periodo diciottennale.
exEn: Nutation superimposes on the Earth's precession a small oscillation with an eighteen-year period.
note: Astronomy/mechanics and botany; Latinism (nutare, to nod). Paired with 'precessione'.

ex: La Terra raggiunge il perielio ai primi di gennaio, in pieno inverno boreale.
exEn: The Earth reaches perihelion in early January, in the depth of the northern winter.
note: Astronomy; opposite 'afelio'. For orbits around the Earth: 'perigeo'/'apogeo'; generic 'periastro'.

ex: La reologia dell'impasto determina quanto il pane lieviterà in forno.
exEn: The rheology of the dough determines how much the bread will rise in the oven.
note: Physics/engineering/food science; adjective 'reologico'. Greek 'rheos' (flow), same root as 'reostato'.

ex: Il senatore pronunciò una filippica di un'ora contro la riforma.
exEn: The senator delivered an hour-long philippic against the reform.
note: Learned (Demosthenes against Philip of Macedon, then Cicero); near-synonyms 'invettiva' (invective), 'diatriba', colloquial 'tirata', 'sfuriata'.

ex: Il vescovo rivolse una severa rampogna ai fedeli che disertavano la messa.
exEn: The bishop addressed a stern rebuke to the faithful who were skipping Mass.
note: Literary; verb 'rampognare'. Scale of reproofs: 'rimprovero' (neutral), 'rimbrotto', 'rampogna', 'reprimenda' (formal), 'ramanzina' (colloquial).

ex: Tornò a casa tardi e si prese i soliti rimbrotti della madre.
exEn: He came home late and got the usual scolding from his mother.
note: Literary-colloquial; verb 'rimbrottare'. Milder and more domestic than 'rampogna'; cf. 'brontolio' (grumbling).

ex: La sentenza è stata pubblicata con numerosi omissis a tutela dei minori coinvolti.
exEn: The judgment was published with numerous redactions to protect the minors involved.
note: Legal/journalistic Latinism, invariable; written '(omissis)' where text is left out. Verb phrase 'omissare' is jargon.

ex: «Salire su» e «uscire fuori» sono perissologie che la lingua parlata tollera.
exEn: 'Salire su' and 'uscire fuori' are redundancies that spoken language tolerates.
note: Rhetoric/linguistics; near-synonyms 'pleonasmo' (the usual term), 'ridondanza'. 'Tautologia' repeats the idea, 'perissologia' adds superfluous words.

ex: Quandanche fosse vero, non cambierebbe nulla.
exEn: Even if it were true, it would change nothing.
note: Literary/formal, takes the subjunctive; also written 'quand'anche'. Neutral 'anche se', 'seppure'.

ex: Le prove erano scarse; cionondimeno la giuria lo condannò.
exEn: The evidence was thin; nevertheless the jury convicted him.
note: Formal/bureaucratic; also 'ciononostante', 'nondimeno'. Neutral 'tuttavia', 'comunque'.

en: with him; with her; with himself (archaic)
ex: Portò seco il figlio minore e lasciò gli altri alla balia.
exEn: He took his youngest son with him and left the others with the wet-nurse.
note: Archaic/literary (Latin secum); the series 'meco, teco, seco'. In modern Italian only 'con sé', 'con lui'. Still heard in 'recare seco'.

ex: Non aveva veruna intenzione di restituire il denaro.
exEn: He had no intention whatsoever of returning the money.
note: Archaic/bureaucratic; used only in negative or interrogative sentences, like 'alcuno'. Forms: veruno, veruna. Manzoni uses it freely.

ex: In siffatte circostanze, ogni ulteriore trattativa sarebbe inutile.
exEn: In such circumstances, any further negotiation would be pointless.
note: Formal/literary (sì + fatto); neutral 'simile', 'tale', 'del genere'. Legal prose still uses it.

ex: Portava una collana di giaietto, nera e lucente come i suoi capelli.
exEn: She wore a necklace of jet, black and shining like her hair.
note: Literary/jewellery term; 'nero come il giaietto'. Cf. 'ebano' (ebony), 'corvino' (raven-black), 'pece' (pitch).

ex: Il vino ha un colore giallo paglierino con riflessi verdolini.
exEn: The wine is straw-yellow in colour with greenish glints.
note: Wine-tasting cliché ('giallo paglierino'); from 'paglia'. Cf. 'dorato' (golden), 'ambrato' (amber).

ex: Un lucore verdastro filtrava dalle persiane socchiuse.
exEn: A faint greenish glow filtered through the half-closed shutters.
note: Literary; weaker than 'chiarore' and 'bagliore', stronger than 'barlume'. From Latin 'lucor'.

ex: Il quadro era appeso a sghimbescio e nessuno se ne accorgeva.
exEn: The picture hung askew and nobody noticed.
note: Colloquial-literary, almost always in 'a sghimbescio' or 'di sghimbescio'; synonyms 'di sbieco', 'di traverso', 'storto' (neutral).

en: hooked; aquiline (of a nose, beak, claw)
ex: Il rapace serrava la preda negli artigli adunchi.
exEn: The raptor gripped its prey in its hooked talons.
note: Literary Latinism (aduncus); 'naso adunco'. Cf. 'uncinato' (hook-shaped, technical), 'aquilino' (of noses only).

ex: La luna gibbosa illuminava il sentiero quanto bastava per non cadere.
exEn: The gibbous moon lit the path just enough to keep us from falling.
note: Learned/astronomical ('luna gibbosa' between half and full); of terrain, 'un terreno gibboso'. Noun 'gibbosità'. Everyday 'gobbo'.

ex: I vaticini degli economisti sulla ripresa si sono rivelati infondati.
exEn: The economists' prophecies about the recovery proved groundless.
note: Literary Latinism (vates, seer), often ironic in journalism; verb 'vaticinare'. Neutral 'previsione', 'profezia'.

ex: Gli storici vedono nelle carestie del 1846 i prodromi delle rivoluzioni del Quarantotto.
exEn: Historians see in the famines of 1846 the forerunners of the revolutions of 1848.
note: Learned (medicine: symptoms preceding a disease; history/politics: precursors); usually plural. Adjective 'prodromico'.

ex: Il mito narra di un'età primeva in cui uomini e dèi sedevano alla stessa mensa.
exEn: The myth tells of a primeval age when men and gods sat at the same table.
note: Literary Latinism (primaevus); near-synonyms 'primordiale', 'primigenio' (original), 'primitivo' (neutral, also pejorative).

ex: Credeva nella gloria immarcescibile dei poeti, non in quella dei generali.
exEn: He believed in the imperishable glory of poets, not that of generals.
note: Literary/liturgical Latinism (from 'marcescere', to rot); 'corona immarcescibile'. Neutral 'imperituro', 'eterno'.

ex: Una subitanea folata di vento spense tutte le candele.
exEn: A sudden gust of wind blew out all the candles.
note: Literary; neutral 'improvviso', 'repentino'. Adverb 'subitaneamente'. 'Subitaneo' stresses the unexpected, 'repentino' the speed.

ex: Il ricordo di quella sera gli tornava ognora alla mente.
exEn: The memory of that evening came back to his mind at every moment.
note: Literary (ogni + ora); found in poetry and formal prose. Neutral 'sempre', 'continuamente'. Cf. 'tuttora' (still).
